The second most important factor was your strong desire to pursue higher education. This actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward passing, since every student who passed also wanted to continue studying. However, its positive effect was not enough to outweigh the other influences.

The third key factor was your level of weekend alcohol consumption, which you described as low. This also nudged the model slightly toward passing, as most students who succeeded reported similarly low or very low weekend drinking.

Although your family situation, study habits, and support network look fairly typical compared with students who passed, the combination of these top influences led the model to recommend extra courses. To improve, consider increasing your weekly study time beyond the two hours you currently spend, since most successful students study 2–5 hours or more. Building consistent study routines now can help turn your clean record and clear ambitions into stronger results. (248 words)
